name: security-llm-fetch-budget-boundaries-review
intent: LLM-driven fetch loops and cost admission at external-tool boundaries
artifacts: Fetch/tool loop implementation, URL policy, budgets, cancellation and per-user charging context.
trace: Trace lower-trust model output into repeated fetch/tool calls and identify admission before each network/cost increment.
experiment: Use local deterministic stub tools with tiny budgets and bounded fixtures; compare normal completion and a loop exceeding the configured count/cost.
disproof: A model suggesting many calls is not resource exhaustion if the orchestrator enforces a budget; do not generate production load.
repair: Enforce cumulative budgets/cancellation at the tool executor and verify useful short tasks and bounded termination.
branch_decisions: Bound the complete tool-call graph, including retries, redirect hops, pagination and nested model invocations, before considering per-request limits. Distinguish a configured authorized budget from a caller ability to exceed it. Use tiny local cost units and deterministic ceilings; do not generate substantial provider charges or infer monetary loss from a long transcript alone.
operational_method: Inspect atomic budget reservation before parallel fan-out, not only a sequential decrement after calls finish. Retain requested, reserved, completed, canceled and reconciled cost units for each child call/retry. In a tiny deterministic fixture start two calls competing for one remaining reservation and verify the configured cap; distinguish asking for cancellation from stopping already charged in-flight work. Never generate significant provider cost for this review.
